item.title: Hong Kong’s ‘patriots only’ polls see 31.9% turnout – up 1.7 % on 2021, but 2nd lowest on record
item.description: Provisional turnout for Sunday’s “patriots only” Legislative Council (LegCo) stands at 31.9 per cent – up 1.7 per cent on the 2021 turnout, though still the second-lowest on record. Candidates had been urging last-minute votes across a city still mourning the worst fire tragedy in decades. Among 4,131,000 registered voters, 1,317,682 cast a ballot in […]

item.title: Tai Po fire: Police oversee overnight removal of flowers, tributes from memorial by volunteers, gov’t staff
item.description: Volunteers and personnel from the Food and Hygiene Department (FEHD) have removed flowers, messages and other tributes for victims of the Tai Po fire under the watch of police officers. item.title: 40 newcomers join Hong Kong’s ‘all patriots’ legislature, Olympic fencer Vivian Kong the youngest
item.description: A total of 40 of the 90 newly elected “all patriots” lawmakers are first-time legislators, with retired Olympic fencing champion Vivian Kong being the youngest in the new legislature. Hong Kong’s second Legislative Council (LegCo) elections, held following the 2021 electoral overhaul, closed on Sunday evening, with a provisional turnout of 31.9 per cent. It […]

item.title: Japan summons China ambassador over fighter jet incident
item.description: By Kyoko Hasegawa Tokyo has summoned Beijing’s ambassador after Chinese military aircraft locked radar onto Japanese jets, the latest incident in the row ignited after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s comments backing Taiwan. Takaichi suggested last month that Japan would intervene militarily in any Chinese attack on the self-ruled island that Beijing claims as its own […]

item.title: Over 3% invalid votes in Hong Kong’s ‘all patriots’ direct legislative polls – new high since Handover
item.description: Hong Kong recorded over 40,000 invalid ballots – or 3.12 per cent of all votes cast in the geographical constituencies – during Sunday’s “patriots only” legislative elections, a new high since the 1997 Handover. item.title: Gov’t social workers ‘did not force’ Tai Po fire victims to vote, Hong Kong’s No. 2 official says
item.description: Government social workers did not force Tai Po fire victims to vote in the “patriots only” legislative elections on Sunday, a top Hong Kong official has said. item.title: Beijing court orders payout for MH370 flight families
item.description: A Beijing court said Monday it had ordered Malaysia Airlines to pay compensation to the families of eight passengers from flight MH370, more than a decade after the plane disappeared. item.description: Every year, Mrs Wong made her daughter a birthday cake, and the family would celebrate her birthday at home. item.title: Families of deadly Tai Po fire victims begin providing DNA samples
item.description: Families of the Tai Po fire victims have started providing DNA samples to help identify their loved ones, as 31 people remain missing nearly two weeks after the deadly blaze. Hong Kong police said they had reached out to families of the missing victims, as well as those who had preliminarily identified bodies through photos. […]

item.title: Scaffold nets removed from 227 Hong Kong buildings; Labour Dept. probes suspected fraudulent safety certificates
item.description: Scaffold nets have been removed from more than 200 premises across Hong Kong under a government order imposed after authorities found suspected forged safety certificates at two sites in the wake of the deadly Tai Po blaze.
